title: Stift Klosterneuburg: A place with a thousand stories | Donau
content: # Klosterneuburg Abbey. **Welcome to Klosterneuburg Abbey and the Order of the Augustinian Canons!**. Just outside Vienna, between the Danube and the vineyards, rises Stift Klosterneuburg Abbey. The Augustinian canons have lived and worked here since the foundation of the monastery. Stift Klosterneuburg is also home to the oldest continuously operated winery in Austria. A visit to Stift Klosterneuburg begins in the Sala terrena, the unfinished garden hall with the monumental atlases by Lorenzo Mattielli. With the Grand Abbey Tour or a wine cellar tour, Stift Klosterneuburg Abbey can be discovered in all its facets - as a historical site, living monastery and traditional winery. As soon as you enter Stift Klosterneuburg Abbey through the Sala terrena, the view of the abbey's diverse garden landscape opens up. It served the canons as a place to relax and is home to one of the largest ginkgo trees in Austria, the neoclassical orangery by Joseph Kornhäusel and a fountain.

Klosterneuburg Abbey is located in Austria. **Klosterneuburg Abbey** (German: *Stift Klosterneuburg*) is a twelfth-century Augustinian monastery of the Catholic Church located in the town of Klosterneuburg in Lower Austria. Overlooking the Danube, just north of the present Vienna city limits at the Leopoldsberg, the monastery was founded in 1114 by Saint Leopold III of Babenberg, the patron saint of Austria, and his second wife Agnes of Germany. The abbey church, dedicated the Nativity of Mary (*Mariä Geburt*), was consecrated in 1136 and remodeled in the Baroque style in the seventeenth century. In 1879, the abbey church and monastery were restored according to plans by Friedrich von Schmidt, and the neo-Gothic twin steeples were erected.
